newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST-Salomon sees '97 Brazil growth at 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Salomon sees '97 Brazil growth at 2.2 pct.

text.p: Brazil's economy will grow by a modest 2.2 percent in 1997 because of constraints imposed by the country's distorted macroeconomic policy, Salomon Brothers said.

"A mix of tight monetary policy, a relatively overvalued exchange rate and a lax fiscal stance will keep Brazil's output below potential in 1997, with growth registering 2.2 percent," Lawrence Goodman, head of Salomon's Latin American economic research, said in a report.
The Salomon forecast is sharply lower than government projections for 4.0 percent to 5.0 percent growth in gross domestic product next year.
Brazil's economy is expected to grow by between 2.5 percent and 3.0 percent this year.

In the report, co-authored by Salomon's Brazil economist Michael Hart, Salomon says Brazil's internal debt will grow next year due to a public sector borrowing requirement in excess of 6.0 percent of gross domestic product.
The country is also expected to experience its fourth current account deficit in 1997, it said.

The report forecasts a current account deficit of 3.4 percent of GDP in 1997, up from a projected 1996 shortfall of 2.9 percent of GDP. It adds that the deficit will constrain GDP targets and limit the prospect for futher appreciation of the real currency as a policy tool.
The report also noted that continued fiscal deficits and a measured depreciation of the exchange rate will lead to high real lending rates.
